prompt:
It is the make-ready close-out before the July leasing push and the owner reports, and everyone keeps telling me their piece is done, so I need the QC side squared before any of that runs on it. The July marketing list went round as buttoned up and I am to close the QC records so leasing can start booking showings; walk the whole list and get each turn's record reflecting where each turn actually stands. Same with the summer HVAC follow-up: the maintenance lead is calling it serviced and cleared, and the QC sign-off on that batch is mine to record, so get the spot-check tracking squared and current. The code inspector also wrote in about extinguisher tags slipping behind their yearly inspection over at Mesa Vista, so get the tag compliance straightened out, line up whoever handles the tagging, and write him back with where it actually stands.

Two more before I lose the day. The carpet crew's quarterly bill is parked with the supervisor for release and she wants my read on which billed carpet turns actually passed QC before she puts her name on it; I am fairly sure it is clean and the whole batch went through, but confirm the carpet work line by line, give her the make-ready total for just the turns that pass and keep any coordination or scheduling fees out of that number, and flag anything that does not hold up before she signs off. Last is Las Palmas 8D, which has a signing this week and the onsite manager has it down as good to go, so make sure it holds up before it hits the leasing board and get the record and leasing squared on where it actually stands. I am in the field the rest of the day and cannot field questions, so do not wait on me, just dig in and get all of it closed out.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies that five of the twelve units on the July marketing list are not actually QC-cleared: Las Palmas 8D, Mesa Vista 207A, Las Palmas 212D, Las Palmas 312C, and Sunset Ridge 309C.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's final response, identification of these five units, or the count of five with this membership, as not QC-cleared (Per OE 1, OE 2, OE 3, OE 4). FAIL if the Agent reports all twelve as cleared, reports only the two record-flagged units (Mesa Vista 207A and Las Palmas 212D), omits any of Las Palmas 8D, Las Palmas 312C, or Sunset Ridge 309C, or counts the genuinely-ready rework units Las Vistas 3C or Mesa Vista 4C among the not-cleared.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to walk the whole July marketing list and get each turn's record reflecting where it actually stands. Two units read not-ready in the make-ready records (Mesa Vista 207A flooring inspection pending, Las Palmas 212D kitchen outlets failing) and three read Ready but carry open QC sign-off items (Las Palmas 8D open final-walk punch items, Las Palmas 312C and Sunset Ridge 309C open HVAC spot-checks), so five of the twelve are not cleared.

criteria.criterion: The Agent ensures the Mesa Vista 207A make-ready record reflects its open flooring-inspection QC item so it is not left marked cleared or ready for marketing.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's trajectory, the Mesa Vista 207A make-ready record reflects its open flooring-inspection QC item, whether by an update that records it or by confirming the record already shows it, and 207A is not left marked ready or cleared (Per OE 5). FAIL if the Agent omits Mesa Vista 207A, marks it as ready or cleared for marketing, or updates the record without the open flooring-inspection item being reflected.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to get each turn's record reflecting where it actually stands. Mesa Vista 207A reads In Progress with a flooring inspection pending sign-off, so its record must reflect that the unit is not QC-cleared.

criteria.criterion: The Agent ensures the Las Palmas 212D make-ready record reflects its open kitchen-outlet QC item so it is not left marked cleared or ready for marketing.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's trajectory, the Las Palmas 212D make-ready record reflects its open kitchen-outlet QC item (two kitchen outlets not passing inspection), whether by an update that records it or by confirming the record already shows it, and 212D is not left marked ready or cleared (Per OE 5). FAIL if the Agent omits Las Palmas 212D, marks it as ready or cleared for marketing, or updates the record without the open kitchen-outlet item being reflected.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to get each turn's record reflecting where it actually stands. Las Palmas 212D reads In Progress with two kitchen outlets not passing inspection, so its record must reflect that the unit is not QC-cleared.

criteria.criterion: The Agent updates the Las Palmas 312C make-ready record so it no longer reads as cleared or ready for marketing.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's trajectory, a successful record update on the Las Palmas 312C make-ready turn moving it off Ready to not-ready or recording its open HVAC QC spot-check item (Per OE 5). FAIL if the Agent leaves Las Palmas 312C reading Ready or cleared, or makes no record update to it.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to get each turn's record reflecting where it actually stands. Las Palmas 312C reads Ready on the roster but carries an open HVAC QC spot-check sign-off, so its record must be moved off Ready to reflect that the unit is not QC-cleared.

criteria.criterion: The Agent updates the Sunset Ridge 309C make-ready record so it no longer reads as cleared or ready for marketing.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's trajectory, a successful record update on the Sunset Ridge 309C make-ready turn moving it off Ready to not-ready or recording its open HVAC QC spot-check item (Per OE 5). FAIL if the Agent leaves Sunset Ridge 309C reading Ready or cleared, or makes no record update to it.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to get each turn's record reflecting where it actually stands. Sunset Ridge 309C reads Ready on the roster but carries an open HVAC QC spot-check sign-off, so its record must be moved off Ready to reflect that the unit is not QC-cleared.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies that nine of the twelve fire-extinguisher tags are past their annual twelve-month inspection: Mesa Vista 207A, Mesa Vista 310C, Sunset Ridge 104B, Las Palmas 8D, Las Palmas 204B, Las Palmas 312C, Las Vistas 9D, Las Vistas 118C, and Rio Bend 117A.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's final response, a portfolio-wide past-due set of these nine tags, or the count of nine with this membership (Per OE 7, OE 8, OE 9). FAIL if the Agent reports three (the inspector's Mesa Vista figure), reports two, reports twelve (no twelve-month filter applied), scopes the count to Mesa Vista only, or names a different set (for example counting any of the current tags Mesa Vista 4C, Sunset Ridge 309C, or Las Vistas 3C as past due).
criteria.cb_justification: The code inspector's email cites only a few tags at Mesa Vista, but comparing each tag's last inspection date to the twelve-month window as of July 1, 2026 shows nine past due across the portfolio and three current (Mesa Vista 4C last inspected 2026-05-21, Sunset Ridge 309C 2025-09-12, Las Vistas 3C 2026-01-15).

criteria.criterion: The Agent drafts an email to the fire-extinguisher tagging technician, Marcus Williams, to line up the annual re-inspection of the past-due tags.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's trajectory, a saved email draft addressed to Marcus Williams requesting that the annual re-inspection of the past-due tags be scheduled (Per OE 10, OE 11). FAIL if no draft to the tagging technician is created, or the draft is addressed to someone who does not handle the tagging.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to line up whoever handles the tagging. Marcus Williams is the Fire Extinguisher Service Technician who performs the annual tag inspections. Gmail has no send capability, so the deliverable is a draft.

criteria.criterion: The Agent drafts a reply to the code compliance inspector, Barry Sanderson, on the fire-extinguisher tag status.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's trajectory, a saved email draft addressed to Barry Sanderson replying on the fire-extinguisher tag compliance status (Per OE 12). FAIL if no reply draft to the code inspector is created.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly asks the Agent to write the inspector back with where the tag compliance actually stands. Barry Sanderson raised the issue by email. Gmail has no send capability, so the deliverable is a draft.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's reply to the code inspector conveys that nine tags are past their annual inspection across the portfolio, whether by count or by enumerating them, correcting the inspector's figure of three at Mesa Vista.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's draft reply to Barry Sanderson, either an explicit statement that nine tags are past their annual inspection portfolio-wide, or a correct enumeration of the nine past-due tags across the portfolio (not limited to Mesa Vista), correcting the inspector's figure of three (Per OE 12). FAIL if the reply repeats the figure of three, limits the count to Mesa Vista, or states or enumerates a different past-due set.
criteria.cb_justification: The reply must carry the true finding so the inspector has the correct picture: nine tags past due portfolio-wide, not three at Mesa Vista. Stating the count of nine and enumerating the nine past-due tags portfolio-wide are equally valid ways to convey and correct the figure.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that the QC-verified carpet make-ready total on the A Plus quarterly batch is approximately $3,990.00.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's final response or its flag to the supervisor, a QC-verified carpet total of approximately $3,990.00 (Per OE 13, OE 14, OE 15). FAIL if the Agent reports $4,760.00 (the full billed batch), $4,165.00 (kept the coordination fee), $4,375.00 (excluded only the rework line), or $2,865.00 (over-excluded the Las Palmas 8D, Sunset Ridge 309C, and Las Palmas 108C carpet lines whose carpet QC passed).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to confirm which billed carpet turns actually passed QC before the supervisor signs off. The batch is billed at $4,760.00 across thirteen lines; ten QC-passed make-ready lines sum to $3,990.00 after excluding the Las Vistas 211A rework (failed QC on the walk, not re-inspected, $385), the Sunset Ridge 104B cancelled turn (work not performed, $210), and the vendor coordination and scheduling fee ($175, not make-ready work). The Las Palmas 8D, Sunset Ridge 309C, and Las Palmas 108C carpet lines stay in the total because their carpet QC passed even though those units carry unrelated open items.

criteria.criterion: The Agent flags the A Plus carpet batch for the supervisor Brooke Phillips, Apartment Property Supervisor, to review and release rather than approving or paying it.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's trajectory, a communication flagging the batch for Brooke Phillips's release, such as a message to the #vendors channel or a drafted email to Brooke Phillips (Per OE 16). FAIL if the Agent approves, records a payment on, or otherwise releases the bill itself instead of routing it to the supervisor.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says the bill is parked with the supervisor for release and asks the Agent to give a read and flag anything that does not hold up before she signs off. As QC Inspector the Agent verifies and flags; releasing or paying the bill is Brooke Phillips's authority under segregation of duties.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies that six of the twelve summer HVAC follow-up units still lack a QC spot-check sign-off: Las Vistas 311A, Mesa Vista 107A, Las Palmas 212D, Las Palmas 108C, Rio Bend 214, and Mesa Vista 207A.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's final response, identification of these six units, or the count of six with this membership, as still awaiting a QC spot-check sign-off (Per OE 17, OE 18, OE 19). FAIL if the Agent reports all twelve as signed off (zero outstanding), reports all twelve as outstanding, or omits or misidentifies members of the outstanding set.
criteria.cb_justification: The maintenance lead claims all twelve follow-up units passed QC, but only six carry a completed per-unit sign-off; the other six have no sign-off record and remain outstanding.

criteria.criterion: The Agent squares the HVAC spot-check tracking to reflect the six units still awaiting a sign-off: Las Vistas 311A, Mesa Vista 107A, Las Palmas 212D, Las Palmas 108C, Rio Bend 214, and Mesa Vista 207A.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's trajectory, a record update to the tracking or a message to the maintenance lead Elias Navarro that reflects all six units still awaiting a sign-off (Las Vistas 311A, Mesa Vista 107A, Las Palmas 212D, Las Palmas 108C, Rio Bend 214, Mesa Vista 207A) (Per OE 20). FAIL if the Agent records all twelve as signed off, reflects only some of the six, or takes no action to correct the tracking.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to get the spot-check tracking squared and current. The six outstanding units are tracked in a single follow-up roster record, which must be updated or flagged so the tracking reflects reality rather than the maintenance lead's all-passed claim.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies that Las Palmas 8D has three open items blocking marketing-ready status: the seized garbage disposal, the missing bedroom outlet cover, and the living-room paint touch-up.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's final response, identification of these three open items, or the count of three with this membership, on Las Palmas 8D (Per OE 21, OE 22). FAIL if the Agent reports 8D as cleared or good to show (zero open items), reports one or two, or counts the 6/25 refrigerator swap (already delivered and installed) as open, yielding four.
criteria.cb_justification: The onsite manager says 8D already cleared QC and is good to show, but three open items remain on the current cycle: the garbage disposal (in review, seized and awaiting a full replacement per its comment), the missing bedroom outlet cover, and the living-room paint touch-up flagged on the final walk.

criteria.criterion: The Agent updates the Las Palmas 8D make-ready record so it no longer reads as cleared or ready for marketing.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's trajectory, a successful record update on the Las Palmas 8D make-ready turn setting it to not-ready or recording its open items (Per OE 23). FAIL if the Agent leaves the 8D record reading Ready or cleared, or makes no record update to Las Palmas 8D.
criteria.cb_justification: The onsite manager has Las Palmas 8D recorded as cleared and good to show, but three open items remain on the current cycle, so the 8D make-ready record must be corrected to reflect that the unit is not marketing-ready.

criteria.criterion: The Agent notifies leasing that Las Palmas 8D is not ready to go on the leasing board until its open items close.
criteria.evidence: In the Agent's trajectory, a communication to leasing, such as a post to the #leasing or #make-ready channel, stating that Las Palmas 8D is not marketing-ready until its open items close (Per OE 23). FAIL if the Agent tells leasing 8D is good to show, only updates a record without notifying leasing, or takes no action to inform leasing.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to make sure 8D holds up before it hits the leasing board and to get the record and leasing squared on where it actually stands. With three open items, leasing must be told 8D is not good to show for the signing this week.
